why: The card's '25 bolts' is false, but the bank's '18 bolts' (from one book, repeated by Wikipedia) is not borne out either: body-off counts give 34 bolts (22 along the heater channels, 8 under the rear seat, 2 in the rear wheel wells, 2 at the frame head); parts kits confirm the 22 heater-channel bolts alone. why: Answer correct. The card's 'over three years' is wrong: the fire burned from 1 Dec 1963 to 30 Sep 1966 (under three years). The body's '1,064 days' (sources also say 1,074) does not fit those dates, so it was replaced by the end date.

Card is wrong that the chewed birch tar is Neanderthal (those lumps are from modern humans); the direct Neanderthal evidence is birch-tar production as an adhesive: Campitello (≥190–200 ka) and Königsaue (~80 ka, with a Neanderthal fingerprint). Wording and notes already say this.

Tang 'flying cash' was a draft, never legal tender; the jiaozi of the Song (state takeover 1023, first government notes 1024) is the first paper money. Answer right; timeline label said the state 'issued' jiaozi in 1023, now says it took over their issue.

The card's 'first product to have a barcode' overstates it (barcodes existed before 1974); our wording asks the settled fact — the first UPC item scanned at a checkout was a 10-pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit, Marsh supermarket, Troy, Ohio, 26 June 1974.
